summary: The Rental Housing Investment Act amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow bonus depreciation for long-term residential rental housing placed in service in the United States after the enactment of the law. Taxpayers can claim a special depreciation allowance for qualifying properties with two or more dwelling units, with higher limits available for properties that meet specific affordable housing requirements.

affected_groups.effect: May make an election to claim bonus depreciation for qualifying residential rental properties placed in service after the enactment date.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers and investors owning long-term residential rental property

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for an increased per-unit deduction limit ($250,000 instead of $150,000) if their property meets specific low-income housing requirements, subject to a 15-year recapture period.
affected_groups.group: Developers and owners of affordable housing projects

key_provisions: Provides a special depreciation allowance for long-term residential rental property equal to the lesser of $150,000 per dwelling unit or 100 percent of the property's adjusted basis (excluding land).
Increases the per-unit limit to $250,000 for long-term residential rental properties that are part of projects meeting specific affordable housing requirements.
Requires property to have at least 2 dwelling units, be placed in service in the U.S. after the enactment date, and have its original use commence with the taxpayer.
Establishes a 10-year recapture period (or a 15-year period for affordable housing properties) where tax benefits are reversed if the property ceases to meet the qualifying requirements.
Treats long-term residential rental property as section 1245 property for recapture purposes.
Specifies that the election to claim the deduction is generally irrevocable without the Secretary's consent.
